title: Rafael and the Typewriter
premise: In the river city of Verensk, Bram Thackeray has passed as a man for five years in her father's print shop, cutting type and keeping quiet while revolution brews. When the bridge closes and soldiers occupy the quarter, Bram discovers her father has been secretly printing a dissident broadside — and he is arrested, leaving the evidence hidden in her hands. With the victors' historians days from writing the official record, Bram must finish and distribute the true account, risking the exposure of both her family and herself. In the end she gets the truth on the record, claims her name publicly, and finds a found family among the printers who choose to stand with her.
about_author: L. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in small-town museums. Their fiction explores the quiet heroism of tradespeople caught in history's margins.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. On the final day before the bridge closes, the city holds its breath; Bram cuts type by lamplight, hiding a growing unease as soldiers arrive and her father burns letters in the stove. When he presses a locked type case into her hands and says only 'remember the order,' Bram realizes the silences she mastered are now a cage. Beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Lead and Ash
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Soldiers arrest her father for sedition, and Bram, alone in the shop, deciphers the locked case: a completed dissident broadside documenting the massacre at the granary, one proof short of a full run. The occupiers' historian arrives to 'correct' the record, offering Bram safety for cooperation. She refuses, and enlists the shop's two apprentices and a widowed bookbinder. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Night Run
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with interludes from the bookbinder Mara. The small crew prints through the night while patrols tighten; a raid nearly catches them, and Mara is wounded covering Bram's escape with the finished sheets. Distributing the broadsides through the closed quarter, Bram is recognized by a soldier from her old life — the one person who could unmask her. Beat: climax, everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Set in Permanent Type
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The broadside spreads faster than the victors can suppress it, forcing an inquiry that frees her father; the soldier who recognized her chooses silence, and Bram, standing before the inquiry, speaks her full name aloud — Bram Thackeray, daughter, cutter of truth in lead. The shop reopens with a new family of printers around her. Beat: belonging claimed, not granted.
